raw_record.question_text: On the provided graph of $G$ vs $f$ (course of reaction), which letter marks the equilibrium position?

method.method_draft: First describe the plotted curve: on the G vs course-of-reaction graph, A and B lie on the descending left side, D and E lie on the rising right side, and C is at the bottom of the curve. Use the rule that equilibrium corresponds to the minimum of Gibbs free energy along the reaction coordinate. Therefore select the letter at the bottom/minimum of the curve: C.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是 Gibbs free energy G 随反应进程 f 变化的曲线，曲线从左侧较高处下降，经过 A、B 附近后到达最低点；字母 C 标在曲线底部的最低位置；之后曲线向右上升，经过 D、E 附近。推理：反应的平衡位置对应 Gibbs 自由能沿反应坐标的最小值。因此最低点处的字母就是平衡位置，即 C。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct thermodynamic-graph method: identify the lowest point of the plotted Gibbs free energy curve and apply the equilibrium criterion for G versus reaction progress.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the graph axes as Gibbs free energy G vertically and course/extent of reaction f horizontally. Observe that the curve decreases from A through B, reaches its minimum at the point labeled C, then rises through D and E.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know the requested quantity is the equilibrium position on a G versus f reaction-course graph, and that the answer should be one of the displayed letters.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For a reacting system at constant temperature and pressure, equilibrium occurs at the minimum Gibbs free energy with respect to reaction progress; equivalently the slope dG/df is zero and G is lowest locally.
